Name: Wall of Undeath
Information:
**Wall of Undeath**

Created from dozens or even hundreds of bodies, raised in a sick mockery of life as a twisting interlocked mass, the wall of undeath is a defense used by necromancers to give purpose to partial bodies and unwanted flesh. They stretch across the important corridors and act as a living gate, which silently waits to devour invaders to add them to its violent mass.

**Structural Weakness.** The wall of undeath counts as a structure to other effects.

**Undead Nature.** The undead does not require air, food, drink, or sleep to survive.

**Quote**

“Life is abundant. Death is unavoidable. Undeath follows both.”

Stat Blocks.title: Wall of Undeath
languages: understands the languages its component bodies knew in life

traits.name: Walled Formation
traits.description:
The wall stretches between two points in its space, each of which must touch another wall (including another wall of undeath) which it adheres to. It perfectly fits against these walls, leaving no space between them: even gasses cannot pass through the wall. If it must detach one of its sides to pivot and attach it to a new wall (such as when moving through a corridor) it must spend an extra 5 feet of movement to do so.

Its maximum length and height is 25 feet, and its body is generally 5 feet thick. It does not fill a cube as creatures regularly do, and instead occupies 5-foot cubes in horizontal and vertical arrangements to represent its height and width. Other creatures that aren’t allied with it cannot pass through those spaces, and everything on one side has total cover against anything on the other. When an ally attempts to move through the undead’s space it must use its action to do so.

When the wall is reduced to 0 hit points it loses its integrity and collapses into pieces in a 20 x 20 ft. cube, which remains as difficult terrain until cleared.

actions.name: Clawing Mass
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +9 to hit, reach 10 ft., targets every creature in range. Hit: 17 (2d10 + 6) slashing damage, and the target is grappled (escape DC 16). Each creature grappled this way takes 6 (1d10) slashing damage at the start of the wall’s turn.

actions.name: Psychic Lure
actions.description:
Each hostile non-undead creature who can see the wall and is within 60 feet of it must make a DC 14 Charisma saving throw. Each creature that fails takes 15 (2d10 + 4) psychic damage and is charmed until the start of the wall’s next turn. Creatures who succeed take half as much damage and aren’t charmed.

A creature charmed by this effect must use as much of its movement as it can to walk toward the wall on its turn, and cannot willingly move away from it or put plans in place to do so.

bonus_actions.name: Subsume Undead
bonus_actions.description: If a willing allied undead, the corpse of an undead, or a corpse that has been dead for more than 10 minutes is within 15 feet of the wall and is smaller than the wall, the wall may pull it into its own body and regain hit points equal to the remaining hit points of that undead (if alive, otherwise regaining 1d8 + 5 hit points), plus another d8 for each size category larger than Medium it is. The wall may target as many undead within range as it wishes to using this action.

reactions.name: Shifting Mass
reactions.description: When one Large or smaller creature attempts to move through the wall’s space, it can allow the creature to pass through without using their own action.
